stories.headline: BofA Sees Oil Around $120 If Iran Resumes Infrastructure Strikes
stories.what_happened: Francisco Blanch, head of commodities and derivates research at Bank of America, discusses the outlook for oil prices after US President Donald Trump says he's weighing further attacks or a resumption of peace talks with Tehran. "If Iran goes back to attacking infrastructure in the region, we think $120 a barrel is probably on the cards on average for the next few months," Blanch tells Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

stories.headline: Sumitomo Life to remain cautious on JGB yields, keep investment pace unchanged from H1
stories.what_happened: Sumitomo Life Insurance will maintain its investment pace for Japanese government bonds in the upcoming months. It intends to carefully monitor yields on super-long Japanese government bonds, assessing any market volatility. The firm expects its JGB holdings to decrease in the Asset Liability Management portfolio by the end of the fiscal year. Predictions suggest that the Bank of Japan will raise its policy rate by December.

stories.headline: French bond selloff eases as country spared ratings downgrade
stories.what_happened: On Monday, the selloff in French government bonds paused after Moody's maintained its rating of Aa3. Weekend protests were mostly peaceful, reducing tensions in the country. France's 10-year OAT yield fell following a rise to its highest level since June 2002. The focus now turns to the European Central Bank's upcoming policy decision on Thursday. Analysts expect the ECB to monitor the rising yields closely and evaluate their impact.

stories.headline: Global Market: BOJ nears historic inflation milestone, shifts focus to rate hikes

With wage growth and inflation expectations strengthening, policymakers may signal further tightening, potentially in December, as they balance persistent price pressures against economic growth and financial stability.
